title: Anyone can trigger an Agent Spell because StarGuard's validation checks make the caller's identity irrelevant
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.3.1.1.2.6 states that "the triggering of an Agent Spell is permissionless; anyone can initiate execution," with a keeper job (StarGuardJob) letting keepers "monitor and execute eligible Spells at the earliest possible block."

That is only safe because nothing about the outcome depends on the caller. A.1.10.2.3.2.3.1.1.2.7.1 lists the checks StarGuard performs inside `exec()`: the whitelisted Spell is "executable only once, enforcing single-use to prevent replay attacks or unauthorized repeats"; the "whitelisted bytecode codehash is valid, protecting against tampering or malicious alterations"; the Spell's own `spell.isExecutable()` view returns true; and "StarGuard retains access to the SubProxy, ensuring no loss of control during the Agent Spell execution."

Each check closes a distinct hole, and together they exhaust what a caller could otherwise influence: *how many times* (single-use), *what code* (codehash), *under what conditions* (isExecutable), and *with what authority* (SubProxy access). With all four fixed at execution time, the caller contributes only the gas and the block.

The `isExecutable()` requirement (A.1.10.2.3.2.3.1.1.2.2) is the notable delegation: Agents write their own execution-time predicate — office hours, expirations, external conditions — and StarGuard enforces it without understanding it. Timing policy stays with the Agent that knows its domain, while the permission to execute stays with the whitelist.

The payoff is liveness. A permissioned trigger makes execution depend on a specific party being available and willing at the right moment; a permissionless one with self-verifying preconditions means an approved Spell executes as soon as it is legitimate, and cannot be quietly stalled by whoever holds the key.
description: Single-use enforcement, codehash match, the Agent's own isExecutable() gate and retained SubProxy access relocate trust from who executes to what the contract verifies at execution time.
